Let’s dive into Chapter 3: Simple Steps for Praying Through the Psalms.
Now that we’ve seen why praying Scripture matters, let’s talk about how you can actually do it—starting with the Psalms. Their honest emotions and poetic words make them a perfect place to begin, no matter your background or experience.
So, how do you pray through a Psalm? It’s easier than you might think. Here’s a simple step-by-step approach:
First, just pick a Psalm. You can follow a reading plan, or you might choose one that fits how you’re feeling today. There’s no right or wrong way—just go with what draws your attention.
Next, read the Psalm slowly and reflectively. Take your time. Pause after a line or a verse. There’s absolutely no rush—this isn’t about checking off boxes, but about letting the words settle in your heart.
After you read a line, respond in prayer. Maybe you want to thank God, or ask for help, or bring up a struggle you’re facing. Sometimes a verse won’t hit home—and that’s okay. Just move on to the next one until something speaks to you.
Flexibility is key. You don’t have to pray through every single verse. If something doesn’t connect, let it go. The goal is to respond honestly and naturally, not to force anything.
And remember, you can continue for as long—or as short—as you’d like. Whether you spend just a few minutes or linger a little longer, you can wrap up and head into the rest of your day whenever you’re ready.
This approach is simple and it’s adaptable. You can try it on your own, with a friend, or even in a group. No special training needed—just a willingness to let the Psalms guide your time with God.
Let’s imagine you’re reading a Psalm that opens with praise for God’s faithfulness. You might pause, think about moments when you’ve seen God come through for you, and thank Him right then and there. Later, maybe you’ll hit a verse about fear or trouble. That’s your cue to bring your own worries or concerns to God, asking for help or comfort.
If you come across a verse that feels distant, don’t worry about it. You don’t have to force a connection. Just move on. The main thing is to respond to what actually speaks to you in the moment.
As you make this a habit, you’ll notice a few benefits. For one, your prayers will get a fresh boost of variety. Each Psalm brings new words, new themes, and new ways to talk to God. You’ll start to understand Scripture more deeply, noticing things you might have skipped over before. And most importantly, your relationship with God will grow more lively and personal—less like a monologue and more like a real conversation.
If you ever struggle with distraction or boredom when you pray, this method can really help. The words of the Psalm give you a gentle guide, keeping your mind focused. And if you do drift off, just return to the next verse and pick up where you left off.
Here’s the best part: you don’t have to stop with the Psalms. Once you’re comfortable, you can use this same approach with other parts of the Bible—stories, teachings, promises. The secret is to come to each passage with an open heart, letting the words shape your prayers.
So, what’s the big takeaway? Praying through the Psalms is a practical, accessible way to breathe new life into your prayers. It blends reading and praying together, helping you build a deeper, more dynamic connection with God—one honest, heartfelt conversation at a time.
